# dtcloud_lb_balancing_pool (Resource)

Builds a listener, its pool, a health monitor and the members in a single call. A create-only shortcut; prefer the granular resources.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The whole chain in one call: listener, pool, health monitor and members.
# Every argument is ForceNew -- changing one rebuilds all four objects.
resource "dtcloud_lb_balancing_pool" "web" {
  lb_id = dtcloud_lb.public.id

  # Front end
  protocol      = "HTTP"
  protocol_port = 80

  # Back end
  backend_protocol      = "HTTP"
  backend_protocol_port = 8080
  lb_algorithm          = "ROUND_ROBIN"

  # Health monitor. `protocol` here is the probe type, not a network protocol.
  health_monitor {
    protocol            = "HTTP"
    url_path            = "/healthz"
    interval            = 10
    timeout             = 5
    healthy_threshold   = 2
    unhealthy_threshold = 3
  }

  member {
    compute_server_id = dtcloud_vm.web.id
    address           = dtcloud_vm.web.primary_ip
    protocol_port     = 8080
  }
}
```

!> **Every argument here forces a new resource.** There is no update endpoint for the chain as a
unit, so changing the probe interval recreates the listener and drops the members with it. Prefer
`dtcloud_lb_listener`, `dtcloud_lb_pool`, `dtcloud_lb_member` and `dtcloud_lb_health_monitor` unless
you specifically want the atomic shape, and never mix the two styles on one load balancer.

## Schema

### Required

- `backend_protocol` (String) Protocol used to reach the members. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `backend_protocol_port` (Number) Port used to reach the members. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `healthy_threshold` (Number) Consecutive successes before a member counts as healthy. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `interval` (Number) Seconds between probes (5-300). Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `lb_algorithm` (String) Balancing algorithm. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `lb_id` (String) ID of the load balancer. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `lb_port` (Number) Front-end port. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `lb_protocol` (String) Front-end protocol. One of: HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, UDP, TERMINATED_HTTPS. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `sticky_session` (Boolean) Whether to pin a client to the member it first reached. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `timeout` (Number) Seconds to wait for a probe response (5-60). Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `type` (String) Health probe type. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `unhealthy_threshold` (Number) Consecutive failures before a member counts as unhealthy. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Optional

- `allowed_cidrs` (List of String) CIDRs permitted to reach the listener. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `certificate` (String, Sensitive) PEM certificate for TERMINATED_HTTPS. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `connection_limit` (Number) Maximum number of concurrent connections. -1 means no limit. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `insert_headers` (Block List, Max: 1) Headers the listener injects into requests forwarded to members. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--insert_headers))
- `member` (Block List) Back-end members created together with the pool. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--member))
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) PEM private key for TERMINATED_HTTPS. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `timeout_client_data` (Number) Client inactivity timeout in SECONDS (note: dtcloud_lb_listener takes milliseconds). Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `timeout_member_connect` (Number) Member connect timeout in SECONDS (note: dtcloud_lb_listener takes milliseconds). Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `timeout_member_data` (Number) Member inactivity timeout in SECONDS (note: dtcloud_lb_listener takes milliseconds). Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `url_path` (String) Path requested by HTTP and HTTPS probes. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Read-Only

- `balancing_pool_id` (String) ID of the balancing pool on its own, without the load balancer prefix.
- `health_monitor_id` (String) ID of the health monitor the platform created.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `listener_id` (String) ID of the listener the platform created.
- `members_state` (List of String) Operating state of each member.
- `members_total` (Number) Number of members in the pool.
- `status` (String) Status reported by the platform.

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **The three listener timings are seconds here**, where `dtcloud_lb_listener` takes milliseconds.
  That asymmetry belongs to the API: this endpoint converts, the listener endpoint does not.
* **Left unset, the platform fills several values in** -- the timings, `url_path` and
  `connection_limit` -- and reports what it chose. They are Computed for that reason; without it an
  omitted value would disagree with the report and, being ForceNew, propose a rebuild on every plan.
* **`health_monitor.protocol` is the probe type**, not a network protocol.

## Timeouts

`create` and `delete` each default to 30 minutes. There is no update.

## Import

```shell
# <load-balancer-id>:<balancing-pool-id>. Import one only when it declares no
# `member` blocks: a member's port is reported by nothing, so declared members
# come back empty and the first plan proposes a rebuild.
terraform import dtcloud_lb_balancing_pool.web 3d372446-4c75-4327-9511-98442456162f:5b2a9c31-7e04-4d88-9c6e-44a2f1d0e7b3
```

`member` blocks do not survive an import: nothing reports a member's port. Import a balancing pool
only when it declares no members, or accept that the first apply rebuilds it.
